claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine your eligibility for Child Benefit. To do this properly, I'll need to ask you some questions about your circumstances and the children you're inquiring about.

Let me start with the first question:

**How many children are you responsible for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm responsible for one child - my son Alex. He's 8 years old and lives here at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know that Alex is 8 years old and lives with you at home.

To continue assessing your eligibility, I need to understand a bit more about your living situation:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you for confirming that. Now I need to understand your immigration or residency status to ensure you meet the eligibility requirements.

**What is your current immigration or residency status in the UK? For example, are you a British citizen, or do you have settled status, pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, or another type of visa or right to reside?**

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent, thank you for that clarification. As a British citizen living in the UK and responsible for Alex who lives with you at home, you meet the key eligibility requirements for Child Benefit.

Let me just confirm one final detail to ensure there are no circumstances that would affect your eligibility:

**Is Alex currently in any of the following situations: in hospital for more than 12 weeks, in care for more than 8 weeks, or receiving certain benefits like Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit in his own right?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, none of those apply. Alex is just living at home with me - he's not in hospital, not in care, and he doesn't receive any benefits in his own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! I have all the information I need to assess your eligibility. Let me now provide you with my findings.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Great news!** You are **eligible for Child Benefit** for your son Alex.

Here's a summary of why:

- ✓ You are a British citizen living in the UK
- ✓ Alex is 8 years old (under 16)
- ✓ Alex lives with you at home
- ✓ You are responsible for Alex
- ✓ There are no disqualifying circumstances affecting Alex's eligibility

You can proceed to make a claim for Child Benefit if you haven't already done so. If you need any further assistance or have additional questions, feel free to ask!
